newsitem.title: UK: Pearson rebounds after management news.
newsitem.headline: Pearson rebounds after management news.

text.p: Shares in media group Pearson Plc recouped Thursday's losses in early trading as investors reassessed reaction to top management changes annnounced yesterday, traders said.
Shares added 12p to 688-1/2p, after falling 11-1/2p on Thursday, on news of the appointment of Marjorie Scardino as chief executive and Dennis Stevenson as new chairman.
But after meeting with the new team last night, analysts said that the market may be preapred to adopt a wait-and-see policy.
"I think she made a very favourable impression but she remains an unproven quality in running a large group," said one analyst at the meeting.

"Her track record at the Economist is very good but it's still a question of seeing what she does when she gets in there. I think she went down well and there will be quite a lot of good will there because people want to see change."

Scardino will replace outgoing chief executive Frank Barlow at the end of year, while Stevenson becomes deputy chairman with immediate effect and will take over as chairman from Michael Blakenham next May.
